title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A retired couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that relied on AI-generated fake website displays showing fictitious account balances. The scammers used an AI system deployed at the presentation layer, after legitimate trading app functionality, to conceal fraud from the user while creating the false appearance of legitimate investment returns and successful withdrawals.

The failure occurred because there was no human verification of account balances or withdrawal requests before funds left the system. The couple saw what appeared to be real transaction confirmations and modest returns early on, which built confidence to invest larger sums. The AI-generated interface mimicked a legitimate trading platform closely enough that deception persisted until a withdrawal request large enough to trigger verification revealed the scheme.

It is not established whether the trading app developers knew their platform was being used this way, or whether the scammers exploited a gap in the app's own controls.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. Jerry Dunaway was initially encouraged to invest small amounts through a mobile trading app, and when he saw modest returns and was able to withdraw funds, he gradually increased his investments. The scammers used an AI-generated fake website that showed fake account balances on his screen, making the scheme appear legitimate while concealing the fraudulent activity.

The couple discovered the scam last week when Jerry tried to withdraw a larger sum and found he couldn't access the money. Gwinnett County police confirmed the app itself was real but had been manipulated by scammers using technology to deceive him. Jerry and Mindy Dunaway are now speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by scammers. Police say victims rarely recover their funds in these cases, and their children have started a GoFundMe to help the couple with daily expenses as they work with investigators.
